text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.99% today to $149.42, continuing a strong two-week run of nearly 5%. The main driver is oil prices themselves: U.S. crude jumped to $107.89 per barrel and global oil to $115.22, fueled by reports on October 28th that the U.S. is preparing for potential Iran strikes after the midterm elections. Higher oil prices directly lift revenues and margins for a major oil producer like this company.

The geopolitical escalation in the Middle East has shifted investor appetite back toward energy stocks. Even as reports emerged that the Iran conflict could cost $47 billion, the market appears to be pricing in sustained elevated oil demand from prolonged regional tension—the kind of scenario that typically benefits large integrated oil producers over a multi-week horizon.
